Wages of Sin

precepts.text: Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body. Reign means rule. Every brother says, I have the porn under control. There is no such thing as controlling sin: once you start obeying that lust, it has you in control. Yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead. For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law of sacrifice, but under grace. What then? Shall we sin because we are under grace? God forbid. Two accounts were told in class of brothers who claimed they had it under control: one was arrested after acting out his compulsion in public in a store, and another crashed his car because he was watching filth while driving. Does that sound like control? You need a checklist in your mind so you can say, I am messed up, I need help, because I could die or end up in jail.
precepts.point: And such were some of you: everybody in here can identify with something on that list and say, I used to do that. But ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God. We are washed with the word of God.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
“Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.” The word reign means to rule: don't let sin rule your mortal body. Every brother says, I got the porn under control, I am in control. There's no such thing as control of sin. Once you start obeying that lust, it has you in control; you don't have it in control.

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.” Men and women are alive from the dead. We have to submit ourselves to Christ; he is our commander, our leader, and what he says we must do.

“For sin shall not have dominion over you”: Paul is reiterating. Dominion goes back to reign in verse 12. “for ye are not under the law”, the law of sacrifice, “but under grace”, the grace of Christ. “What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace?” Should we keep watching porn because we're not under the law of sacrifice? “God forbid.”

One brother said, I got it under control. In a store, thinking about porn, he was on his phone looking at it, forgot where he was, took his pecker out and started looking at all the ladies. Does that sound like he had it under control? He got arrested; he's in jail. Another decided to look at porn while he drove home, and bam, he crashed. It has you in check. You need a checklist in your mind so you can say, I'm messed up, I need help, because I could die or I could be in jail. That is sin reigning, and the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom.

precepts.text: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. What you put in, you are going to receive as a reward.
precepts.point: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap. When you put in the sin, the consequences are going to happen. For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption: you will be judged by it. But he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting: when you sow yourself into the scriptures, the Lord gives blessings, favor, mercy, and abundance.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
“whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.” What you put in, you are going to reap. When you put in the sin, the consequences are going to happen, period. Paul says it plainly: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Sin is death. That is the corruption reaped by the one who sows to his flesh: sow that sin to your flesh and you will be judged by it. And the gift of God, eternal life through Christ, is the “life everlasting” reaped by the one who sows to the Spirit.

What you put in, you are going to receive as a reward. Wages for sin, a gift for the one who sows to the Spirit. God is not mocked.

precepts.text: What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death. The fruit of the things you now realize were sinful behavior ends in death. He is dealing with the carnality.
precepts.point: To be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace. Notice it is not just life, it is peace. You know why some of you still have so much drama in your lives? Because you are not applying this. You have no peace because you are trying to seek peace in things that are not God. The Bible talks about God's perfect peace, the peace of God which passeth all understanding: it will overcome anything you are dealing with. If it does not seem to work for you, you are still not applying what you need to apply.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
“For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh”. Where your heart is, there will your treasure be: if you are after the flesh, you are going to mind the things of the flesh. “For to be carnally minded is death”. If you stay in that carnal mind, that is death.

Romans 6 goes with it: “What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed?” That is the fruit of the things you now realize were sinful behavior. “for the end of those things is death”. The end of the things you should be ashamed of is death. Paul is dealing with the carnality.

So the death of Romans 8:6 is not a mystery: it is the fruit of minding the flesh. The things we once did in the flesh bore nothing but shame, and their end is death.

Then read Romans 8:5 again with that in mind: “but to be spiritually minded is life and peace”. Notice it is not just life; it is peace. Some of us still have so much drama in our lives because we are not applying this, seeking peace in things that are not God.

precepts.text: Answer D is a scary mindset to have. What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? That is the mindset of the Christian church: I found grace, grace covers me, I can do what I want as long as I believe; I do not have to do what Christ says. That is a terrible mindset, and it is exactly what this verse is warning against.
precepts.point: Correct answer read: the real battlefield is private. A lot of people fall spiritually in secret long before they fall publicly. The representative shows up at the Sabbath; the real you shows up when you are at home, when you are alone, when you are with your family. Your wife knows exactly who you are. You cannot come up here saluting hard like you are over righteous and then go home and verbally, financially, or physically abuse your wife: you lack integrity and you have poor character. And vice versa, sisters: you cannot bow all the way down at the door and then go home and curse your husband out and keep nothing. You lack integrity in that area too.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

precepts.why:
The question put to the class: you're alone online late at night, temptation hits, and nobody from the congregation would know. What shows integrity? A, entertain the temptation privately. B, watch a little and justify it later. C, cut it off immediately and fight temptation. D, convince yourself grace covers everything. Answer D is a scary mindset to have, and Paul already answered it: “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?”

Shall we continue in sin that grace may cover everything? That is a terrible mindset, and it is the mindset of Christianity: I found grace, grace covers me, I can do what I want when I want. All I have to do is believe in Jesus; I ain't got to do nothing he says, just believe he's my Lord and savior. Christianity is evil.

The answer is C. The questions are easy and the answers are easy; the problem is when it comes to fruition in real time. You are fighting your war against yourself: you don't want to push play, but you want to push play, and nobody is there to tell you a damn thing. That is when C gets blurred out.

The real battlefield is private. A lot of people fall spiritually in secret long before they fall publicly. The representative shows up at the Sabbath; the real you shows up at home, alone, with your family, and your wife knows exactly who you are. You can't salute so hard you're over righteous and then go home and verbally, financially or physically abuse your wife. And sisters, you can't bow 90 degrees at the door and then go home, cuss your husband out, and keep a filthy house. That is lacking integrity and poor character.

That is Proverbs 11:3: “The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.” Grace is not a cover for sin; integrity is acting on what you know, even when nobody is watching.

precepts.text: The earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God; the creature itself shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. That's our expectation. So if we know the wages of sin is death, then why sin? Then you're not expecting this. In that day he's going to say, I never knew you; you didn't do what I said to do. How do you expect something you didn't do?
precepts.point: The wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. The payment for sin is death. Through Christ is eternal life; isn't that what we're looking for? If we keep the commandments, we are expecting the kingdom.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
“For the wages of sin is death”. The payment for sin is death. “but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord”. Through Christ is eternal life, and that is what we are looking for. If we keep the commandments, God says he is going to give us the kingdom, so we are expecting the kingdom.

Romans 8 shows that expectation: “For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” The creature “was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope”, “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.” That is what our expectation is to be: delivered out of bondage into the liberty of the children of God.

Then if we know the wages of sin is death, why sin? If you live in sin you are not expecting this; you know what you are going to get. In that day you will be saying Lord, Lord, and he will say, I don't know you; you didn't do what I said to do. How do you expect something you did not do?

So if your expectation is to be called a son of God in the kingdom, do not let sin reign in this mortal body. The one living a life of sin and thinking he will go to the kingdom is not going; he will be in the lake.

precepts.text: The Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered: that part of us that groans to God because we're expecting the kingdom, if we're sincere. All things work together for good to them that love God: if you love God, you are keeping the commandments. Whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son: you're going to measure to the fulness of the stature of Christ in this mortal body, because sin cannot reign in this mortal body. Stop thinking it happens on the other side; whoever couldn't figure out that you cannot live a life of sin and enter the kingdom is going to the lake. A hard word with it: sisters that are married, if you refuse to reverence your husband and live to his guidance in the Lord, no head covering or office covers that. And husbands, if you're not guiding your wife and molding your house in these scriptures, that's on you; you're no wise master builder, and the children pay for it. When a child in a covenant house is deep in uncleanness, something is wrong in that house.
precepts.point: Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead. Because you're expecting the kingdom.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
“Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.” That is the part of us that groans to God because we are expecting the kingdom, if we are sincere. We are asking God to deal with us: I want the kingdom, I don't want to come up short, Lord, please preserve me, help me. Then let the word be engrafted in your mind; he is telling you what to do.

“And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.”

“And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God”. If you love God, you are keeping the commandments. It works for good to those keeping the commandments, those that have the word engrafted in them, “the called according to his purpose.”

“For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son”. Those that followed him before will follow him again; they are predestinated. You are going to be conformed to that image and measure to the fulness of the stature of Christ in this mortal body, because sin cannot reign in this mortal body. Stop thinking it is going to happen on the other side. Whoever could not figure out that you cannot live a life of sin and go to the kingdom is not going; they are going to be in the lake.

A hard word goes with it. Sisters that are married: if you refuse to serve your husband, look at him as your lord and obey him, down to the little things he tells you to do, you are not going, no matter how many head covers you wear or what offices you hold. If Jesus told you, you would do it. And husbands, if you are not guiding your wives in these scriptures and showing them how to be that woman, that is your fault; you are no wise master builder, having expectations while not molding them. Then the children are cursed. When a twelve-year-old in the house is deep in gay porn, something is wrong in that house, something is wrong with those parents.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord, who is our Passover, who set the example. That is the promise made to Abraham, for us to get repentance for sins.
precepts.point: Whosoever eateth leavened bread, that soul shall be cut off from Israel: how do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps in your mind and you say, I do not like that brother; you are spiritually consuming it. That is how you get cut off from your people. This is a serious thing.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Exodus 12:15 says, “whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.” What is that really saying? How do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps into your mind and you say, damn, I don't like that brother. You are spiritually consuming it, entertaining sin and not purging the leaven from your house. That is how you get cut off from your people, and this is a serious thing.

How you get cut off: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Christ is our Passover, who set the example. That is the gift, the promise made to Abraham, for us to get repentance for sins, because we are in a wicked place.

And Exodus 13:7 says “there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters.” We do not want to be seen in the midst of sin, Passover or not. Don't be the brother who does not throw the bread out but puts it in his storage closet and brings it back when Passover is over: laying the bitterness aside for the season and picking right back up hating the brother. That is not the spirit. Throw it out. Let it go.

precepts.text: The law and the testimony: the form of doctrine delivered to us.
precepts.point: God be thanked that ye were the servants of sin but have obeyed from the heart the doctrine delivered you: you understand your mission, as Bishop Kani said, the crown is already yours and it is for you to keep it on your head.

note.label: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.why:
“Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” That is the million-dollar question: who do you give your service to? Money? The spirit of fornication? Alcoholism? The big-mouthed black woman that sleeps right next to you? Weakness as a man? Fear? Satan whispering that God can never use you because of your past? When you come into this truth and apply it, you are a new creature; old things are passed away.

“But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.” What is that form of doctrine? “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.” The law and the testimony, the commandments and the testimony of Christ, is the doctrine delivered to us, and we obeyed it from the heart.

Thank God you understand your mission. You have your crown; it is already there, and it is for you to keep it on your head. You erase yourself out of the book of life; you are already ordained to get it. Will you hold on? “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

Your opponent is not the brothers that look like you. First it is the man in the mirror, and sin is the op. Use this Bible to shoot down all sin that opposes you, and put your energy there. Many cannot function without an oppressor, because with freedom comes change and responsibility. Choose this day who your Lord is: sin unto death, or obedience to the law and the testimony unto righteousness.

precepts.text: Let not sin reign in your mortal body; yield your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.
precepts.point: I will render double unto thee: for your shame ye shall have double, everlasting joy, and your seed known among the Gentiles, so that all who see your children acknowledge them as the seed the Lord has blessed. Write the chain of events: awakening, tribulation, World War III, Armageddon where Christ makes his advent, deliverance, wilderness, kings and priests.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
If sin is the prison, Paul tells us how to walk out of it: “Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.” Don't let sin reign, meaning rule, within you.

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.”

Our bodies must be vessels of righteousness, used for the commandments of God and nothing else. That is how the prisoners of hope turn to the stronghold: no longer servants of sin, but instruments of righteousness unto God.

precepts.text: Sin shall not have dominion over you, for ye are not under the law of sacrifice but under grace; shall we sin then? God forbid. His servants ye are to whom ye obey, and if you wake, work and sleep thinking of porn, that is your god.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
When you keep entertaining a sin, it binds you. Paul says, “For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.” We are not under the law of sacrifice, but under grace. “What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.”

“Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” His servants ye are to whom ye obey. If you wake up thinking about porn, go to work thinking about porn, and go to sleep thinking about porn, that is your god. You are its servant.

Grace is not a license to keep sinning; it is so that sin shall not have dominion over you. Christ laid down his life so we could fight to stop sinning, not so we could be bound in it. And when you are bound, there is no magic scripture that will release you; you have to want to be released.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death.
precepts.point: Keep my commandments and live. Whoever does not keep the law will not live.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

precepts.why:
And what does sin pay? “For the wages of sin is death”. So eating pork is going to kill you. Overeating is going to kill you. Aren’t you supposed to be the temple of God? If you keep eating a certain way, you are destroying yourself, and God will destroy him that destroys the body.

If you do not care about the vehicle the Most High gave you, how will you do the job we are all called here to do? When it is time for missions you cannot go. Brothers over a certain weight class cannot go to camp, and many will fall out of the truth over it: first staying home, then every week a different story, sick, the sniffles, until they find out they love food more than they love the Lord. God forbid something pops off at camp and you become a liability.

As we prepare for the end, get your eating under control. They can starve you for five days, then put you in a room with a Thanksgiving dinner, and you will spill your guts, just as in the Maccabees they tried to make them eat pork. If you cannot control yourself around a slurpee, you will betray this truth for fried chicken.

The law is holy, and keeping it is life; transgressing it is sin, and the wages of sin is death. We warn you because we are trying to save your life. When the high cholesterol, the high blood pressure and the diabetes hit you, you will remember these classes.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ. Sin entered when Adam hearkened to his wife, and death with it; the gift comes after we pass through that covenant, and pride will keep us from it.
precepts.point: Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly. If God has revealed himself to you, humble yourself before the King of kings.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Why do we die? We try to break it down so the new people coming into the faith can put the puzzle together: “For the wages of sin is death”. That is why the covenant, thou shalt die the death, passed upon all of us. When Adam listened to his wife Eve and consented to the idolatry she brought to him, sin came into the world, and when sin came, death came with it.

“but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” That is what we get in the repentance. But we still have to go through the covenant of all flesh. You can't receive the gift of eternal life while you are still in the flesh; flesh and blood cannot enter into the kingdom of heaven. We have to pass through that covenant.

And one thing we had better make sure we don't have on us when we leave this body is pride. That will keep us out of it for sure. That is why Paul says not to think of yourself more highly than you ought: the one who dies like the beasts receives the gift only through Christ, and only if he goes to his grave humble.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ; that is the grace, that we are not killed for our sins.
precepts.point: By grace ye are saved means all of us deserve death for our sins, but through Christ we have grace and are saved from the destruction to come, if we endure to the end keeping the commandments.

note.label: Leviticus 7: Christ Our Peace Offering

precepts.why:
Paul says “the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

That is the grace: we are not killed for our sins. The trespass offering, one law with the sin offering, most holy, is what stood between the trespasser and death; now the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ, if we endure to the end keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death; sin is what brings the cursing and the death.
precepts.point: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded which Joshua read not before all the congregation, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them: those were the strangers that fell in line with Israel, with the fear of the Lord in them, as Rahab had.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why: “For the wages of sin is death”. The cursings Joshua read are what sin brings; sin is what brings the cursing and the death. Life is the keeping of the commandments, death is the wages of sin, and the Most High left that one thing optional: blessing or cursing, life or death. Choose life, for it is not just you that pays but thy seed as well.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death; that has always been the case for the Israelites.
precepts.point: The hidden ones are the key. When you learn your true identity you change your life: less pornography, less marijuana, less going to the doctor, less mass incarceration, no eating pork, no celebrating Christmas or the fourth of July. That repentance is where your power lies, and that is why they work to keep you asleep.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David understands the sign of the times. He says “if there be iniquity in my hands”, if he has “rewarded evil unto him that was at peace with me”, then “Let the enemy persecute my soul, and take it; yea, let him tread down my life upon the earth, and lay mine honour in the dust.” If he is wicked, God's punishment is just.

Paul lays down the rule David is going by: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” That has always been the case for the Israelites. If you are breaking the law, getting arrested is just. If you are selling drugs to your people, it is just a matter of time before a rival riddles your trap with bullets. If we are wicked, the evil happening to us is just.

The gift of God is eternal life through Christ, but it comes to those who turn from the sin that earns death.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death; through sin death came into the world, and our forefathers understood this.
precepts.point: The pants your grandma loved wearing, the auntie who thinks she can teach in the church, standing before the scriptures with a covered head, men and women with the head wrong; we set light by the Commandments as if these are small things. We sinned against the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Through sin death came into the world. Our forefathers understood this. The slave ships, being shot down in the streets, the curses: these are the wages of sin, because we sinned against the Most High.

David keeps his sin ever before him because he knows what sin pays. Acknowledging our transgressions is how we turn from the wages of sin to the gift of God, eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

precepts.text: Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? God forbid; how shall we that are dead to sin live any longer therein?
precepts.point: Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
This is after the death of Christ, under grace, and Ananias was put to death for lying and breaking his vow. “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?”

Grace was never a licence to sin. Those who are dead to sin do not live any longer in it, and Ananias shows what happens under grace to the man who does.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
precepts.point: Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

The wages of sin is death, even now, after Christ. Ananias earned those wages at the apostles' feet, and great fear came on all that heard it.

precepts.point: Proverbs 24:16 also applies: a just man falls seven times and rises up again.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Paul answers the same question the same way in Romans: “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?” God forbid.

You cannot take advantage of grace and continue breaking the law. Seeking to be justified by Christ does not make Christ the minister of sin; grace is not a license to keep transgressing the law.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 2 Message to the 7 Churches

precepts.why: “the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life”. Eternal life is what we want. The elect in the first resurrection have already been judged and do not have to fear the second death. If relatives rejected the truth and died in their sins, their relationship to us does not exempt them from the later judgment.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

points: Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness. Whatever you decide to do, you become that servant. As long as you are serving sin, you are serving sin unto death; that is the road you are heading down.
